correctness.rationale: Read frozen RESULT.md and checker.py; the cut coarea identity bounds the weighted TV of every vertex permutation by max J_k/I_k, and linear interpolation between f and g decomposes nonlinear sorting into finitely many such permutations. Strict-ranking f and f+1_S witnesses attain each cut ratio. Singleton and doubleton cuts force equal weights on all possible edges at L=1, including n=2 separately. Path/cycle/star/barbell evaluations agree with the cut formula. Independent exact weighted four-vertex cut enumeration gave ratios (4,10/3,4); checker.py was inspected (not blindly used). No universal assertion rests on the finite checks.

value.rationale: The two-input stability modulus of graph rank sorting, which is not implied by one-input Pólya–Szegő contraction, has a sharp finite combinatorial characterization for arbitrary positive edge weights, a rigidity theorem, and a quadratic barbell counterexample. Such a parameter quantifies sensitivity of graph-variation regularization and is not a routine relabelling.

final_claim: For every finite connected positive-weighted simple graph, the exact two-input total-variation Lipschitz coefficient of global coordinate rank sorting is max_{1<=k<n} J_k/I_k, with sharp fixed-rank witnesses; equality one holds precisely for equal-weight cliques, and a q-clique barbell has floor(q^2/2)+1.
